blocks.explanation:
\({}^{10}P_{5}\) counts the arrangements of 5 things chosen from 10 different things.
We must find its value.
Plan: use \({}^{n}P_{r} = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\), cancel, and multiply 5 numbers counting down from 10.
steps:
Given: \(n = 10\), \(r = 5\).
To find: \({}^{10}P_{5}\).
Method: \({}^{n}P_{r} = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\). After cancelling, it is the product of \(r\) numbers counting down from \(n\).

Cancel \(5!\)
\[= \dfrac{10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5!}{5!}\]
\[= 10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6\]
Why: \(10! = 10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5!\), so the \(5!\) on top and bottom cancels.

Multiply
\[10 \cdot 9 = 90,\quad 90 \cdot 8 = 720\]
\[720 \cdot 7 = 5040\]
\[5040 \cdot 6 = 30240\]
Why: Multiply two at a time and keep a running total.

Check
Box method: 5 places with 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 choices.
\[10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 = 30240 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \({}^{n}P_{r}\) always has exactly \(r\) factors; here 5 factors.

blocks.explanation:
\({}^{5}P_{2}\) counts arrangements of 2 things out of 5.
We must find its value.
Plan: formula, cancel \(3!\), multiply the 2 top numbers.
steps:
Cancel and multiply
\[= \dfrac{5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3!}{3!}\]
\[= 5 \cdot 4 = 20\]
Why: \(5! = 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3!\); the \(3!\) cancels, leaving 2 factors.

Check
2 places: first has 5 choices, second has 4.
\[5 \times 4 = 20 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Once one thing is placed, only 4 remain for the second place.

blocks.explanation:
Here \(r = n = 7\): all 7 things are arranged.
We must find \({}^{7}P_{7}\).
Plan: use the formula with \(0! = 1\), so the answer is \(7!\).
steps:
Use the formula
\[{}^{7}P_{7} = \dfrac{7!}{(7-7)!} = \dfrac{7!}{0!}\]
\[= \dfrac{7!}{1} = 7!\]
Why: \(0! = 1\) by definition; this is exactly why the book defines it so (\({}^{n}P_{n}\) must equal \(n!\)).

Check
7 places with 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 choices give \(5040\) \(\checkmark\)
Why: Arranging all \(n\) things gives \(n!\) ways.

blocks.explanation:
\({}^{10}P_{3}\) counts arrangements of 3 things out of 10.
We must find its value.
Plan: formula, cancel \(7!\), multiply 10, 9, 8.
steps:
Cancel and multiply
\[= \dfrac{10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7!}{7!}\]
\[= 10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 = 720\]
Why: The \(7!\) cancels; 3 factors remain because \(r = 3\).

Check
Box method: \(10 \times 9 \times 8 = 720\) \(\checkmark\)
Why: 3 places with 10, 9 and 8 choices.
